title: Multinomial Logistic Regression Aanalysis
text:
The analysis uses a restricted participant-level dataset preprocessed by YuFong. The dataset is stored separately from this public repository. Authorised researchers can supply its external file path through the CDP_DATA_PATH environment variable. See the data availability and privacy statement for handling requirements.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(nnet)
library(epiDisplay)
library(lmtest)
library(gt)




Code
data_path <- Sys.getenv("CDP_DATA_PATH")

if (!nzchar(data_path)) {
  stop("Set CDP_DATA_PATH to the restricted dataset outside this project.")
}

data_path <- normalizePath(data_path, mustWork = TRUE)
project_dir <- Sys.getenv(
  "QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR",
  unset = normalizePath("../..", mustWork = TRUE)
)
project_dir <- normalizePath(project_dir, mustWork = TRUE)

if (
  identical(data_path, project_dir) ||
    startsWith(data_path, paste0(project_dir, .Platform$file.sep))
) {
  stop("CDP_DATA_PATH must point outside the public website project.")
}

analysis_variables <- c(
  "N_Diabetes_WHO", "N_DIABETES_2b", "PRS_tertiles",
  "coffee_tertiles", "SEX", "Age", "bmi", "NIT_alcoholtot",
  "smoking_3cat", "mean_step_min_wake_T", "DHD_sum", "NIT_kcal",

data <- read_csv(
  data_path,

WarningMissing data



I’m not sure how Yufong dealt with the missing data. Here, I remove the subject’s data if he/she has at least one missing value (denoted by NA, -999, or -888) in the selected 20 variables.
There is another issue if we want to make model selection or comparison by AICs or likelihood ratio tests, we need to have the same data (after removing the missing) when fitting to each model.








ImportantQuestions




What is the reason that we make PRS and Coffee variable from a continuous scale to three ordinal categories (low, medium, and high) for each? Why not four or more, or just keep it continuous? I think it needs more explanation (Testing for trend).
Does it have any advantage of using tertiles to separate three categories?

title: Multinomial Logistic Regression Aanalysis
text:
2.1 Models
The dependent variable has three (ordinal?) categories. It is usually to use oridinal logistic regression to fit the data. One of the assumptions underlying ordinal logistic (and ordinal probit) regression is that the relationship between each pair of outcome groups is the same. In other words, ordinal logistic regression assumes that the coefficients that describe the relationship between, say, the lowest versus all higher categories of the response variable are the same as those that describe the relationship between the next lowest category and all higher categories, etc.

H0: Parallel Regression Assumption holds


However, we found the assumption does not hold in our data. because it did not pass the parallel ratio check (link)?
Therefore, we tried to use
\[
\begin{align}
\log\left(\frac{p_{\text{Pre}}}{p_{\text{NGM}}}\right) = \alpha_{1} + \beta_{11} E_1 + \gamma_{11} C \\
\log\left(\frac{p_{\text{T2DM}}}{p_{\text{NGM}}}\right) = \alpha_{2} + \beta_{21} E_1 + \gamma_{21} C
\end{align}
\]

Now, I reproduce Table 4 in the paper
To illustrate how to calculate the odds(-like) ratios in two categorical exposure variabes, I take Model prs_cof1 for example. The model for Pre vs. NGM is
\[
\ln\left(\frac{p_{\text{Pre}}}{p_{\text{NGM}}} \right) = \alpha_{11} + \beta_{11} \text{CoffeeMedium} + \beta_{12} \text{CoffeeHigh} + \beta_{13} \text{PRSMedium} + \beta_{14} \text{PRSHigh} + \gamma_{11} \text{Age} + \gamma_{12} \text{SexFemale}
\]
Let $l_{} = $ , where \(C \in \{\}\) for Coffee and \(Y = Y The general odds ratio formula is:\)$ OR = e^l. \[
and the 95% CI of OR is:
\] (1-)%~CI = e^{l Z_{1-/2}} \[
where the variance of $l$ is
\] Var(l) = $$
If I want to know the OR when Coffe level is medium and PRS level is high, it means
\[
\text{CoffeeMedium} = \text{PRSHigh} = 1 \quad \& \quad \text{CoffeeHight} = \text{PRSMedium} = 0
\]

  T2DM_prs_cof3 = map2_chr(PRSlevels, Coflevels, ~ get_OR_CI(prs_cof3_ml, "T2DM", c(.x, .y))))

gt(prs_cof_OR_table,
   rowname_col = "PRS_levels",
   groupname_col = "Cof_levels", 
   row_group_as_column = TRUE) |>
  tab_stubhead(label = c("Coffee", "PRS")) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Pre", columns = starts_with("Pre")) |>

  cols_label(ends_with("1") ~ "M1",
             ends_with("2") ~ "M2",
             ends_with("3") ~ "M3") |>
  fmt_markdown()

title: Diabetes and polygenic-risk analysis: data availability and privacy
text:
The participant-level dataset used for this analysis is restricted and is not distributed with this public website repository.
The file contains individual-level health, demographic, behavioural, medication, socioeconomic, and polygenic-risk variables. Whether any subset may be shared depends on the original consent, data-use agreement, ethics approval, and applicable institutional requirements; repository publication should not be assumed to be permitted.
For local reproduction by an authorised researcher, store the dataset outside the repository and provide its path through the CDP_DATA_PATH environment variable. The analysis rejects paths inside the website project. Do not copy or commit the participant-level file anywhere in this repository.
Only variables required by the published analysis are loaded. Public outputs should contain aggregate summaries and model results rather than participant-level records.
